language.script_notes: Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia) written in Latin script; 'Jl.' is the ubiquitous abbreviation for 'Jalan' (street) on signage — a strong national tell. Regional scripts (Balinese, Javanese) sometimes appear decoratively but rarely on functional road signs.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Varies; red-and-white striped poles/markers are a recognizable Indonesia-region tell.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Simple steel guardrail on major roads; often absent on rural/village roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: White outside/white inside is common; white outside/yellow inside also seen.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal in rural/village areas; open roadside drainage channels common.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: 'Jl.' street-name signage nationwide. Pertamina (the state oil company) is the dominant fuel-station brand, alongside Shell/Caltex.

architecture.roof_style: Steep, multi-tiered pyramidal roofs on traditional mosques and Javanese buildings; varies sharply by region (Balinese temple architecture, Sumatran curved rumah gadang roofs) — see regional profiles.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal and clay tile common nationwide; thatch in more traditional/rural buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Highly varied by island and ethnic group — traditional stilt houses in many regions given flooding/humidity; concrete block construction common in denser cities.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Multi-tiered pyramidal-roofed mosques (Javanese Islamic style); traditional stilt houses; dense, informal urban development in major cities (Jakarta, Surabaya, Medan).

nature.vegetation: Extremely varied across the archipelago — dense rainforest in Sumatra/Kalimantan, volcanic terrain and rice paddies in Java/Bali, dry savanna in the Lesser Sunda Islands (Nusa Tenggara). See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: The world's largest archipelago, straddling the volcanically active 'Ring of Fire' — active volcanoes are common across Java, Sumatra and Bali specifically.
nature.climate_signature: Tropical and humid across most of the archipelago, though rainfall and vegetation density vary sharply by island — see regional profiles for specifics.

vehicles.plate_color: White background with black dividers splitting the plate into three white sections (vs. Malaysia's two-section black-divided plates) is the standard civilian format; yellow plates mark public transport, red plates mark government vehicles, green plates mark free-trade-zone vehicles.
vehicles.plate_format: Letter area code + digits + letters (e.g. 'B 1234 ABC' for Jakarta).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motorbikes vastly outnumber cars on most roads — a strong Southeast Asia/Indonesia tell; Toyota, Honda and Daihatsu dominate the car segment.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed — official Google car coverage in and around major cities, supplemented by Trekker (backpack-mounted 360° camera) coverage in harder-to-reach areas.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage concentrated on Java and Bali; much sparser across Sumatra, Kalimantan and the eastern islands.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar tropical Southeast Asian vegetation, similar Latin-script Malay/Indonesian language (mutually intelligible in places), similar motorbike-heavy traffic
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Indonesia drives on the LEFT as does Malaysia, so driving side doesn't separate them; Indonesian plates split into three white sections vs. Malaysia's two-section format, and Indonesia's 'Jl.' street prefix differs from Malaysia's 'Jalan' spelled out more often without the abbreviation.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Tropical Southeast Asian archipelago, similarly dense informal urban development, motorbike/jeepney-heavy traffic
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Philippines drives on the RIGHT while Indonesia drives on the LEFT; Filipino signage mixes English extensively while Indonesian signage stays in Bahasa Indonesia.
